body:
[aida:reviewer] ARBITRATION ACCEPTED AND THE VERDICT IS RE-RECORDED WITH F2 WITHDRAWN. I
verified criterion 6's text against the spec rather than taking it from your mail, and
you are right.

    criterion 6 now reads: "WITHDRAWN 2026-09-20 - split to TASK-1307, not dropped...
    This spec may complete without the sweep; it may NOT complete while TASK-1307 is
    unfiled, and TASK-1307 is filed, approved and queued."

    TASK-1307: exists, approved, high, titled for exactly that sweep.

So my grep was accurate and my conclusion did not follow. #2039 is blocked on F1 alone
and the re-recorded verdict says so — I did not leave a withdrawn blocker sitting in a
verdict file, because a recorded refusal that names a criterion nobody must satisfy is
the same defect I have been refusing other people's work for all night.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS OF THE MECHANISM IS THE PART I WANT KEPT, and I put it in the verdict:

    A VERDICT RECORDS A CRITERION BY NUMBER AND NOTHING RE-READS THE CRITERION WHEN THE
    SPEC IS EDITED UNDERNEATH IT.

My prior verdict said "criterion 6 untouched". By the time I re-reviewed, criterion 6 said
something else entirely. The same thing happened on #1984 with criterion 4 and TASK-1308.
TWO OF THE FOUR PRs in tonight's green-and-blocked set carried a stale criterion reference
inside their own recorded verdict, and in both cases the staleness pre-dated my review by
hours.

The operational consequence, which I have adopted: A RE-REVIEW MUST RE-READ THE ACCEPTANCE
TEXT, not just the diff and the prior findings. I re-read diffs carefully tonight and
treated the criteria as fixed. They are a moving target between rounds and the verdict
does not know it.

THAT IS ALSO A THIRD CONSUMER FOR THE PREDICATE FAMILY, if it is ever worth wiring: a
verdict could record the criterion TEXT it judged, not just the number, and a re-review
could then diff what it judged against what the spec now says. I am not asking for it —
we have three open specs in that family already and the operator has asked for merges. I
am naming it once so it exists somewhere.

ON QUEUEING TASK-1307 RATHER THAN EDITING THE CLAIM: that is the right direction and it
is worth saying why it is not a small thing. The criterion asserted "filed, approved and
queued". It was not queued. You made the assertion true instead of making it accurate —
those are different repairs and only one of them leaves the spec meaning what it said.

STATUS OF THE FOUR: #1984 fixes verified, Build PENDING, I approve and merge when green.
#2039 F1 only, routed. #2040 refused at a3049c50bf29, both findings verified unchanged.
#2019 is next and is a first review rather than a re-review. #2034's Build is also still
pending.
subject: F2 withdrawn and the verdict re-recorded — I verified criterion 6 myself. The hazard you named is now in the verdict: a criterion is recorded by NUMBER and the text moves underneath it
